extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / graduate students and researchers in functional analysis, PDEs, and Sobolev spaces
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and related results for deciding when a family of functions in Lp (on RN or on finite-measure subsets) has compact closure (strong topology), plus related compactness/weak-compactness, convolution, and functional-analytic facts used in proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascoli–Arzelà criterion for compactness in C(K)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let K be a compact metric space and H a bounded subset of C(K). Assume H is uniformly equicontinuous, i.e., ∀ε>0 ∃δ>0 such that d(x1,x2)<δ ⇒ |f(x1)−f(x2)|<ε ∀f∈H. Then the closure of H in C(K) is compact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is given as the model result for strong compactness in a space of continuous functions; it motivates the 'integral equicontinuity' condition used later for Lp. See references (Rudin, Knapp, etc.) for proof and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kolmogorov–M. Riesz–Fréchet criterion (Theorem 4.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let F be a bounded set in Lp(RN) with 1 ≤ p < ∞. Assume that lim_{|h|→0} ||τ_h f − f||_p = 0 uniformly in f∈F, i.e., ∀ε>0 ∃δ>0 such that ||τ_h f − f||_p < ε ∀f∈F and ∀h with |h|<δ. Then the closure of the restrictions F|_Ω in Lp(Ω) is compact for any measurable set Ω⊂RN with finite measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the Lp analogue of Ascoli–Arzelà: the translation-continuity (an 'integral equicontinuity') plus boundedness gives total boundedness on finite-measure sets. The text gives a four-step proof using mollifiers ρ_n, estimates (showing ρ_n * f approximates f in Lp uniformly on F), boundedness/Lipschitz estimates on ρ_n * f (to apply Ascoli on a bounded subset ω), truncation to a set ω of finite measure to control tails, and assembling finite ε-covers. See Steps 1–4 in the proof for explicit construction and constants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation: translation-uniformity is 'integral equicontinuity'
rubrics_metrics.description: Assumption (22) (translation continuity in Lp uniformly on F) should be compared with the pointwise modulus-of-continuity (21) in Ascoli; (22) is an 'integral' equicontinuity assumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use (22) as the right notion of equicontinuity in Lp. The proof shows how mollification converts this integral equicontinuity into uniform equicontinuity on compact sets (after truncation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mollification estimates used in compactness proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Given mollifiers ρ_n and f∈F, one has ||ρ_n * f − f||_p → 0 uniformly in f∈F for n large (Step 1), and bounds: ||ρ_n * f||_∞ ≤ C_n ||f||_p and |(ρ_n * f)(x1) − (ρ_n * f)(x2)| ≤ C_n ||f||_p |x1 − x2| (inequalities (24) and (25)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These estimates provide uniform boundedness and equicontinuity (on bounded sets) needed to apply Ascoli–Arzelà to the family of mollified functions restricted to a bounded set. Constants C_n depend only on n and the mollifier; Hölder and derivative bounds are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tightness condition for compactness in Lp(RN) (Corollary 4.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let F be a bounded set in Lp(RN) with 1 ≤ p < ∞. Assume (22) (uniform translation continuity) and, in addition, ∀ε>0 ∃ bounded measurable Ω ⊂ RN such that ||f||_{Lp(RN\,Ω)} < ε ∀f∈F. Then F has compact closure in Lp(RN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The extra condition (27) is a tightness (vanishing tail) requirement that ensures compactness on the whole RN rather than only on finite-measure restrictions. The text shows lifting compactness of restrictions to compactness in the full space by zero-extension of approximating centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convolution with fixed L1 kernel yields compact families (Corollary 4.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let G∈L1(RN) and F = G * B where B is a bounded set in Lp(RN) with 1 ≤ p < ∞. Then F|_Ω has compact closure in Lp(Ω) for any measurable Ω with finite measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces the translation continuity of f=G*u to the translation continuity of G: ||τ_h f − f||_p ≤ C ||τ_h G − G||_1, so Lemma 4.3 (continuity of translations in Lq) applies. This is a common technique: convolution with a fixed L1 kernel regularizes and yields compactness on finite-measure sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation continuity for Lq functions (Lemma 4.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If G ∈ Lq(RN) with 1 ≤ q < ∞, then lim_{h→0} ||τ_h G − G||_q = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses density of C_c in Lq: approximate G by G1∈C_c and use uniform continuity of translations on compactly supported continuous functions. This lemma is often used to establish (22) for convolutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remark: practical method for checking compactness in bounded Ω
rubrics_metrics.description: When trying to establish F has compact closure in Lp(Ω) with Ω bounded, it is convenient to extend functions to all of RN, apply Theorem 4.26, then consider restrictions to Ω.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a practical recipe: use extension + Kolmogorov–Riesz to reduce to the whole-space hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Egorov's theorem (Theorem 4.29)
rubrics_metrics.description: On a finite measure space, if f_n→f a.e. then ∀ε>0 ∃ measurable A with |Ω\A|<ε such that f_n→f uniformly on A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Egorov is used frequently to pass from almost-everywhere convergence to uniform convergence off a small-measure set; useful in compactness/approximation arguments (see Exercises and Remarks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dunford–Pettis characterization of weak compactness in L1 (Theorem 4.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let F be a bounded subset of L1(Ω). Then F has compact closure in the weak topology σ(L1,L∞) iff F is equi-integrable, i.e., (a) ∀ε>0 ∃δ>0 such that ∫_A |f| < ε ∀A measurable with |A|<δ and ∀f∈F, and (b) ∀ε>0 ∃ ω⊂Ω measurable with |ω|<∞ such that ∫_{Ω\ω} |f| < ε ∀f∈F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the correct notion of weak compactness in L1: equi-integrability (tightness + control on small sets). The text references Dunford–Schwartz and Diestel for proofs and probabilistic aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding L1 into Radon measures and weak (vague) compactness
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify L1(Ω) with a subspace of M(Ω) (Radon measures) via Tf(u)=∫_Ω f u dx. M(Ω) (dual of C(Ω)) has compactness properties in the weak-* topology; bounded sequences in L1(Ω) have subsequences converging to Radon measures in σ(M(Ω),C(Ω)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This embedding explains how L1 sequences can converge (vaguely) to measures such as Dirac masses; useful when classical weak compactness fails in L1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Riesz representation theorem for Radon measures (Theorem 4.31)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every continuous linear functional μ on C(Ω) (a Radon measure) is given by integration against a unique signed Borel measure ν: ⟨μ,u⟩ = ∫_Ω u dν ∀u∈C(Ω).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies the dual of C(Ω) with (signed) Radon measures and underpins the previous identification of L1 as a subspace of M(Ω). A variant holds for C_0 spaces with boundary measure zero condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bochner Lp spaces: reflexivity condition
rubrics_metrics.description: For a measure space Ω and Banach space E, Lp(Ω;E) consists of measurable E-valued functions with ∫ ||f(x)||^p < ∞. If E is reflexive and 1<p<∞, then Lp(Ω;E) is reflexive and its dual is Lq(Ω;E*).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fact is used to import reflexivity/compactness arguments to vector-valued settings (e.g., evolution equations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Riesz–Thorin interpolation (Theorem 4.32)
rubrics_metrics.description: If T is a bounded linear operator T:L1(Ω)→L1(Ω) with norm M1 and T:L∞(Ω)→L∞(Ω) with norm M∞, then for every 1<p<∞, T is bounded on Lp(Ω) and ||T||_{L^p→L^p} ≤ M1^{α} M∞^{1−α} for the appropriate interpolation exponent α (standard Riesz–Thorin/Marcinkiewicz interpolation estimate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This result allows transfer of operator bounds from endpoints (L1 and L∞) to intermediate Lp spaces; references and classical proofs are given. It is a central tool in harmonic analysis and PDE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Young's convolution inequality (Theorem 4.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f∈Lp(RN), g∈Lq(RN) with 1≤p,q≤∞ and 1/r = 1/p + 1/q − 1 ≥ 0, then f * g ∈ Lr(RN) and ||f * g||_r ≤ ||f||_p ||g||_q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to control convolutions and show they map bounded sets to bounded/compact sets when combined with other hypotheses; proof refered to Exercise 4.30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and equivalent criteria of equi-integrability (Exercise 4.36)
rubrics_metrics.description: A subset F⊂L1(Ω) is equi-integrable if (a) F bounded in L1, (b) ∀ε>0 ∃δ>0 s.t. for measurable E with |E|<δ one has ∫_E |f| < ε ∀f∈F, and (c) ∀ε>0 ∃ω⊂Ω measurable with |ω|<∞ such that ∫_{Ω\ω} |f| < ε ∀f∈F. Equivalently, (d) lim_{t→∞} sup_{f∈F} ∫_{|f|>t} |f| = 0 and (e) lim_{n→∞} sup_{f∈F} ∫_{Ω\Ω_n} |f| = 0 for an exhaustion Ω_n↗Ω.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are practical criteria to verify equi-integrability; part of the Dunford–Pettis theory. The exercise also asks to show compact ⇒ equi-integrable (and consider converse).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vitali convergence theorem (Exercise / Egorov + equi-integrability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vitali-type statement: if (f_n)⊂Lp(Ω) is equi-integrable (control on small measure sets) and f_n→f a.e., then f∈Lp(Ω) and f_n→f in Lp(Ω).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as Exercise 4.14 (part 4) combining Egorov and equi-integrability hypotheses. Useful to deduce strong convergence from a.e. convergence plus uniform integrability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projection onto closed convex set in Hilbert spaces (Theorem 5.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let K⊂H be nonempty, closed and convex in a Hilbert space H. For every f∈H there exists a unique u∈K minimizing ||f−v|| over v∈K (u = P_K f). Moreover u is characterized by u∈K and (f−u, v−u) ≤ 0 for all v∈K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two existence proofs are given (via reflexivity/uniform convexity and via a direct Cauchy-sequence argument using the parallelogram law). The variational inequality (f−u, v−u)≤0 is the standard characterization used in projection and optimization arguments in Hilbert spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hilbert spaces are uniformly convex and reflexive (Proposition 5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Hilbert space H is uniformly convex (consequence of the parallelogram law), and thus H is reflexive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform convexity is shown by the parallelogram law and yields reflexivity; this structural fact underpins existence of minimizers and compactness arguments relying on reflexivity.
